- projection (dimension reduction when embedding equations as curves)
- constraint enforcement that identifies states (like periodic closure conditions)
- unobserved degrees of freedom (hidden variables in the rolling system)
- dissipative elements (even tiny ones break invertibility)
- quotienting by symmetry (holonomy often effectively does this)

- fully explicit
- deterministic
- geometrically well-defined

and still non-invertible.

- embedding into curves
- projecting onto constrained manifolds

Every step must preserve distinguishability between all possible inputs.
